description:
Forty-three recorded name-and-place keys hold two flows on the build of 30 August 2026, and they are genuine disagreements between merged lists: `Carbon dioxide` in unspecified air is fossil carbon to BAFU and Stepwise and land-use-change carbon to ecoinvent, because ecoinvent spells fossil out as `Carbon dioxide, fossil` and distinguishes this variant by identifier alone. No rule derives an answer, so the recorded-by-name tier declines them.

#864: a caller whose source_label names a merged list has supplied the missing fact -- whose vocabulary the row speaks -- so the named list's own recorded ruling answers its ties, reported with the competing flows beside it. This file claims the premise as data: most of the disagreements are settleable that way, because at least one list is unanimous at almost every conflicted key. The behavioural half -- Stepwise's label turning unqualified carbon dioxide fossil -- is held by tests/test_lookup_recorded.py against the real build.

expectations.title: A caller naming their lineage could settle most of the recorded disagreements
expectations.comment: 34 of the 43 conflicted keys on the 30 August 2026 build have at least one merged list that is internally unanimous, which is what source_label arbitration requires. The other nine are lists disagreeing with themselves, which no lineage settles and nothing should.
